matches.rationale: No finding points to the selective reporting of FID scores in the abstract that omits poor results at higher replacement ratios. The available findings address different FID range discrepancies or unrelated issues.

Prediction 7 highlights confusion in Equation 2 regarding the definition of L_reg and its relationship to the regression loss, matching the ground truth's criticism that the equation's notation and the role of the regression objective are unclear.

No finding identifies missing hyperparameter specifications (scheduler warm-up details, clip norm target, batch-size ambiguity) in the experimental protocol. The related data/iteration issue in prediction 8 addresses a different table and experiment.

The overstatement in the introduction about 'proves to be a lightweight approach' and 'utility in short- and long-context settings' is not captured by any finding; the closest (prediction 2) targets a different factual error, not the exaggerated claim of general applicability.

Prediction 4 identifies that Table 4 uses '✗' to indicate failure (FID > 50) yet still reports ΔFLOPs values, aligning with the ground truth's concern about omitting actual FID while continuing to list efficiency metrics, and the resulting ambiguity.
Prediction 9 points out that footnote 1 attributes a theoretical foundation for grafting to a plant biology paper (Goldschmidt), exactly the fabrication of relevance that the ground truth describes.
The problematic interpretation of the locality metric L_k (band‑k locality averaged over positions) is not mentioned in any finding.

The unfair comparison in the PixArt‑Σ evaluation (baseline sampling steps and LoRA usage not controlled) is not addressed by any finding; the available finding about Table E.1 concerns training data amount, not experimental fairness.
No finding captures the misleading comparison in Table 6 where the grafted model’s higher parameter count (712M vs. 340M) is not acknowledged when claiming superiority over pruning baselines.

The omitted limitations in the conclusion (catastrophic failure at 100% replacement, artifacts in PixArt‑Σ) are not identified; prediction 3 describes different overstatements (universal solver, universal outperformance) that do not match the ground truth's omission issue.

The ground truth concerns the selective reporting of latency measurements with a non‑standard batch size (2) and missing throughput/utilization data. No finding addresses batch size or missing efficiency details; prediction 1 reports a different inconsistency (speedup values mismatch).
The compute claim (<2% pretraining compute) and its inconsistency with the 10% vs 20% data usage and best‑result configuration are not flagged by any finding.

The introduction’s promotional language ('revolutionary', 'paradigm shift', 'unprecedented') is not detected by any finding; existing findings refer to other overstatements or factual errors in different sections.
The flawed FLOP formula for softmax attention in Appendix H.1 and its impact on reported ΔFLOPs percentages are not discussed in any finding.
The misrepresentation of reference [52] (progressive network grafting for few‑shot classification) as prior work on architectural editing in generative models is not mentioned in any finding.
